quirks: The named RAG Web Browser actor (apify/rag-web-browser, API id apify~rag-web-browser) runs in Apify Standby mode and returns HTTP 400 {error.type: actor-standby-not-supported-for-agentic-payments} when called via run-sync with x402/agentic payment. Apify charged the $1 USDC anyway.
Do NOT retry this specific actor over x402 run-sync — payment is taken but the call always fails. Money is lost on each attempt.
The :actorId path segment uses the Apify ~-encoded actor id (owner~name), e.g. apify~rag-web-browser, not a slash.
Only non-standby Apify actors are compatible with this run-sync x402 surface; this registry entry points at a standby actor and is non-functional as configured.
usage.guide: Do not use this endpoint as registered: the RAG Web Browser actor is an Apify Standby actor and run-sync rejects agentic/x402 payments with HTTP 400 (actor-standby-not-supported-for-agentic-payments) AFTER charging $1 USDC. The generic POST https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/:actorId/run-sync mechanism likely works for non-standby actors (fill :actorId with the owner~name form and pass that actor's input JSON), but the specific apify~rag-web-browser actor here is incompatible and only loses money. Treat as broken until repointed to a non-standby actor.
